subject: Linguistics
title: Denotation and Connotation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Denotation and Connotation.

hook.text: 'Cheap' and 'affordable' denote the same thing—low cost—but they feel completely different.

buildup.text: Denotation is a word's core dictionary meaning; connotation is its emotional coloring.

discovery.text: Advertisers exploit connotation: 'pre-owned' sounds better than 'used,' though both mean the same.

twist.text: Connotations shift across cultures—'blue' signals sadness in English but immortality in Korean.

climax.text: Choosing words is often about choosing connotations—the emotional payload matters as much as the fact.

punchline.text: Same fact, different word, different feeling.

quiz.question: What is connotation?
options: The emotional or cultural associations of a word
